resolved_positions.topic: Mandatory compliance domains for regulated CDS
resolved_positions.consensus: Regulated CDS must address: quality management (QSR/ISO 13485 + IEC 62304 software lifecycle), clinical evidence (validation, real-world performance), premarket submission (510(k) or De Novo), labeling (intended use, limitations, warnings), cybersecurity (risk assessment, SBOM), and post-market surveillance (MDR adverse event reporting, change control).
Regulated CDS must document decision-making logic, input data requirements and quality specifications, and performance characteristics — not just outputs. This is distinct from general labeling.

resolved_positions.topic: FDA CDS exemption criteria under 21st Century Cures Act
resolved_positions.consensus: CDS software is exempt from FDA medical device regulation only if it meets ALL four criteria: (1) not intended for acquiring/processing/analyzing medical images or in vitro diagnostic signals; (2) intended to display, analyze, or print medical information about a patient or peer-reviewed clinical data; (3) intended to support or provide recommendations to a healthcare professional about prevention, diagnosis, or treatment; (4) intended to enable the HCP to independently review the basis for recommendations so that it is not the sole basis for clinical decisions.
CDS software must satisfy ALL four criteria simultaneously to qualify for exemption. Failure to meet any single criterion subjects the software to FDA medical device regulation.
The unifying theme across all criteria is that CDS must support — not replace — clinician judgment. The HCP must be able to independently review the basis for any recommendation.

All three models agree that healthcare professionals must be able to independently review the basis for CDS recommendations — the 'black box' logic must be accessible and understandable to clinicians.
Exempt CDS must be directed at healthcare professionals, not patients, and must support rather than replace clinical judgment.

CDS software that directly acquires, processes, or analyzes medical images or in vitro diagnostic device signals does NOT qualify for exemption and remains subject to FDA oversight. GPT omitted this; Claude and Gemini both explicitly included it.

510(k) requires a legally marketed predicate device and demonstrates substantial equivalence; De Novo is for novel low-to-moderate risk devices with no predicate, requiring independent safety/effectiveness evidence and resulting in a new device classification.
510(k) targets ~90-day review; De Novo targets ~120-day review, with additional pre-submission steps. Both can run longer due to FDA information requests.
A granted De Novo creates a new Class I or II classification with special controls, and the cleared device becomes a valid predicate for future 510(k) submissions, enabling follow-on innovation.
Companies may attempt 510(k) first and pivot to De Novo if no suitable predicate is found. De Novo also confers a competitive advantage by establishing the first predicate in a new device category.

resolved_positions.topic: Core content requirements for legally-defensible UTI discharge block

Recognition Latency is the elapsed time between when information becomes available post-snap (defensive coverage, open receivers, pressure) and when a quarterback initiates a decision response. It is a cognitive-processing metric distinct from physical execution metrics.
Lower recognition latency correlates with higher completion percentage, lower sack rate, lower interception rate, and higher EPA. It is most predictive of QB performance under defensive pressure.

Recognition Latency cannot be measured directly with publicly available data. Analysts rely on proxies: time-to-throw, pressure-to-sack ratio, Next Gen Stats time-under-pressure, and subjective film study. Each proxy conflates QB cognition with play design and protection quality.

Recognition Latency requirements are system-dependent. Quick-pass, West Coast, and no-huddle offenses demand lower latency than pro-style or play-action-heavy systems, making it a relevant variable in QB-scheme matching.

Recognition Latency cannot be measured directly in real-time match play; analysts must use proxy measures including video timestamp analysis, GPS/optical tracking data, eye-tracking in training environments, and cognitive testing.

Experience level, tactical knowledge, physical fatigue, pressure, positioning, and cognitive abilities all modulate Recognition Latency, with veteran players and well-positioned players showing lower latency.
Recognition Latency data applies to player development training design, positional-specific coaching, substitution timing, and recruitment evaluation for high-tempo systems.

RL is a time-based cognitive metric measuring the gap between when critical game information becomes available (snap, motion, formation reveal) and when a player demonstrates appropriate response through movement or positioning. It is one of four core cognitive metrics in the Third & 20™ system alongside Assignment Accuracy (AA), Leverage Integrity (LI), and Situational Decision Index (SDI).

RL is derived from game film using computer vision (YOLOv8 + ByteTrack) to track player movements and correlate them with play events. Timeframes range from milliseconds to approximately 2-3 seconds depending on play complexity.

RL provides 'why' intelligence behind player decisions rather than 'what happened' statistics. High RL (slow recognition) indicates cognitive processing gaps addressable through film study; Low RL combined with High Leverage Integrity indicates instinctive, sound players.

When opponents show consistently high RL against specific formations, Third & 20™ should generate formation-specific play suggestions (e.g., 'Call bunch concepts — their safety is 0.8 seconds slow to rotate'). This is the differentiator from descriptive platforms like Hudl.

No single statistic tells the complete story of defensive performance. Effective evaluation requires combining traditional stats, advanced analytics, and contextual factors such as strength of schedule, game script, and offensive support.

Pipe-created subshells breaking variable scope (pipe while-loop vs process substitution), unquoted variable word-splitting, and function/PATH shadowing of common binaries are the three highest-confidence stump patterns. evolving_frameworks.name: Folklore-vs-Technology Confusion Pattern
evolving_frameworks.description: A failure mode where a model, given a culturally meaningful name (e.g., Anansi, Hermes, Oracle), defaults to inventing a plausible modern AI product rather than correctly identifying the cultural referent. Components: (1) culturally loaded name as input, (2) model confabulates a tech product, (3) correct model identifies cultural origin. Signals the need for ground-truth anchoring in swarm memory for named entities.

evolving_frameworks.name: Information Preservation Spectrum
evolving_frameworks.description: A conceptual axis from ancient oral knowledge systems (Anansi-style storytelling: cultural wisdom, moral lessons, community transmission) to modern AI documentation tools (DAX-style scribing: clinical accuracy, structured data, workflow efficiency). Useful for positioning new tools and clarifying their genealogy and purpose.

evolving_frameworks.name: CDS Regulatory Risk Ladder
evolving_frameworks.description: A tiered model with four rungs: (1) General wellness/informational — fully exempt; (2) Decision-support with mandatory HCP review — likely exempt but monitor guidance updates; (3) Recommendation-generating CDS without HCP override mechanism — De Novo or 510(k) required; (4) Autonomous/adaptive clinical decision systems — highest scrutiny, AI/ML SaMD action plan applies. Rung assignment drives the entire compliance obligation stack.

evolving_frameworks.name: Compliance Obligation Stack
evolving_frameworks.description: Layered structure where each higher-risk classification adds obligations without removing lower-tier ones: Base layer (all CDS) = labeling + interoperability + data security; Layer 2 (regulated device) adds QMS + clinical validation + premarket submission; Layer 3 (post-market) adds MDR reporting + change control + performance monitoring; Layer 4 (adaptive algorithms) adds predetermined change control plans + continuous real-world evidence.

evolving_frameworks.name: CDS Exemption Gate Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Four sequential Boolean gates that CDS software must all pass to avoid FDA device regulation: Signal Exclusion Gate (no medical image/signal acquisition) → Information Display Gate (displays patient or clinical data) → HCP Recommendation Gate (supports, not replaces, professional judgment) → Independent Review Gate (HCP can audit the basis for recommendations). Failure at any gate reclassifies the software as a regulated device.

evolving_frameworks.name: CDS Exemption Layered Gate Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Gemini surfaced a two-layer structure: Layer 1 = three universal disqualifiers/requirements (no direct image/signal processing; transparent logic; clinician-judgment-support intent); Layer 2 = software must fall into at least one of four permitted functional categories (display, guideline recommendations, interpretation aids, population comparison). Failing any Layer 1 gate means no exemption regardless of Layer 2 fit.

evolving_frameworks.name: FDA CDS Risk Gradient
evolving_frameworks.description: A spectrum where higher-risk CDS (direct signal/image processing, autonomous treatment decisions) remains under full FDA device regulation, while lower-risk CDS (transparent, clinician-reviewed, evidence-based support tools) qualifies for exemption. The four criteria function as a risk-threshold filter rather than a binary category.

evolving_frameworks.name: FDA Device Pathway Ladder
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-tier regulatory framework ordered by novelty and evidence burden: 510(k) at base (predicate-dependent, equivalence standard, lowest cost/time) → De Novo in middle (no predicate, risk-benefit standard, creates new classification and special controls) → PMA at top (high-risk Class III, full clinical trials, highest cost/time). De Novo acts as a bridge that converts novel devices into future 510(k) predicates, collapsing the ladder for follow-on entrants.

evolving_frameworks.name: Anansi Discharge Document Architecture
evolving_frameworks.description: Each diagnosis document has two layers: (1) Static prose blocks — legally reviewed, model-synthesized full paragraphs covering diagnosis explanation, medication compliance, improvement timeline, self-care, culture follow-up, return criteria, and emergency criteria; these never change per patient. (2) Variable fill-in fields — medication name, dose, frequency, duration, lab turnaround, provider contact info, patient identifiers — populated at point of care, ideally via EHR automation. Legal defensibility depends on the static layer being locked and the variable layer being accurately completed.

evolving_frameworks.name: Multi-Model Synthesis Quality Hierarchy for Clinical Documentation
evolving_frameworks.description: When synthesizing clinical prose from multiple AI models, assign each model a domain strength: GPT for patient-facing clarity and readability, Claude for legal comprehensiveness and medication compliance depth, Gemini for implementation scaffolding and operational considerations, Grok for emergency criteria specificity and provider accountability language. The final document pulls from domain leaders rather than averaging all outputs. Conflicts (e.g., fever thresholds) are flagged as unresolved and escalated to clinical or legal authority rather than arbitrarily resolved.

evolving_frameworks.name: Safety Anchor Pattern
evolving_frameworks.description: Emergency criteria sections must contain five non-negotiable safety anchors for any infection-based diagnosis: (1) fever with chills above a defined threshold, (2) organ-specific pain indicating upward spread (flank pain for UTI signaling kidney involvement), (3) inability to take oral medication or fluids, (4) neurological change (confusion, altered mental status), and (5) systemic infection signs (sepsis indicators). Any discharge template missing one of these anchors is considered incomplete for legal defensibility purposes.

evolving_frameworks.name: Recognition Latency Decomposition Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-stage cognitive pipeline for QB decision-making: (1) Pre-snap encoding — reading defensive alignment and forming coverage hypotheses; (2) Post-snap disambiguation — updating hypotheses as routes develop and defenders react; (3) Execution trigger — initiating throwing motion once a target is confirmed. Recognition Latency is the cumulative delay across stages 2 and 3; pre-snap work can compress stage 2 latency, which is why time-to-throw is a biased proxy.

evolving_frameworks.name: Latency-Scheme Fit Matrix
evolving_frameworks.description: A two-axis framework mapping QB recognition latency (fast to slow) against offensive system demand (high-speed precision timing vs. patient pro-style reads). QBs in the high-latency/high-demand quadrant show the greatest performance degradation; QBs in the low-latency/low-demand quadrant may be underutilized. Scheme changes that shift demand axis can mask or expose latency problems.

evolving_frameworks.name: Cognitive vs. Physical QB Evaluation Split
evolving_frameworks.description: Separates QB evaluation into two orthogonal axes: cognitive metrics (recognition latency, decision accuracy, coverage ID rate) and physical metrics (arm strength, release mechanics, mobility). A QB can score well on one axis and poorly on the other. Recognition latency sits entirely on the cognitive axis, meaning it can be high even when traditional stats look strong if the QB is being schemed open rather than reading the field.

evolving_frameworks.name: Three-Phase Recognition Latency Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Decomposes Recognition Latency into Perception (identifying the relevant cue), Processing (interpreting the situation and selecting an action), and Reaction (initiating the physical response). Each phase has distinct measurement handles: eye-tracking for Perception, decision logs for Processing, movement data for Reaction.

evolving_frameworks.name: Proxy Measurement Stack for Cognitive Metrics
evolving_frameworks.description: A layered approach to measuring non-observable cognitive constructs in live sport: Layer 1 = in-game tracking data (coarse, continuous), Layer 2 = video annotation (precise, manual), Layer 3 = controlled lab/VR testing (direct but low ecological validity). Validity claims require triangulation across layers rather than reliance on any single method.

evolving_frameworks.name: Third & 20™ Cognitive Quartet
evolving_frameworks.description: Four-metric cognitive profile system: Recognition Latency (how fast a player sees it), Assignment Accuracy (whether they know what to do), Leverage Integrity (whether they play sound positional football), and Situational Decision Index (composite cognitive score). Each metric diagnoses a distinct failure mode; their combination produces the SDI card used for prescriptive coaching intelligence.

evolving_frameworks.name: RL Diagnostic Cross-Matrix
evolving_frameworks.description: Two-axis diagnostic framework combining RL with other metrics to classify player cognitive profiles: High RL + Low AA = sees it but doesn't know the assignment; Low RL + High LI = instinctive sound player; High RL + High LI = slow but scheme-sound; Low RL + Low AA = fast reactor with knowledge gaps. Each quadrant maps to a distinct coaching intervention.

evolving_frameworks.name: Four-Phase Solo-Dev Retrieval Ladder
evolving_frameworks.description: A progression for resource-constrained developers: Phase 1 — conditional sections in a single context file (hours, low maintenance, medium scalability); Phase 2 — keyword-indexed snippet injection before querying (days, low maintenance, medium scalability); Phase 3 — Google Drive API integration with automated ranking and logging (weeks, medium maintenance, high scalability); Phase 4 — full RAG pipeline with embeddings and vector DB (months, high maintenance, very high scalability). Each phase produces operational value and generates data that informs the next phase.

evolving_frameworks.name: Token Budget Allocation Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Partition the context window into three named zones: Core Zone (20-30% for boot_context.md baseline), Retrieval Zone (up to 20% for dynamically injected snippets, hard-capped per snippet at 500-1000 tokens), and Live Zone (remaining capacity for the current query and model response). Retrieval failures fall back to Core Zone only, never expand into Live Zone.

evolving_frameworks.name: Three-Tier Defensive Evaluation Stack
evolving_frameworks.description: Layer 1 (Essential): counting stats that are universally understood — points, yards, turnovers, sacks. Layer 2 (Advanced): efficiency-adjusted metrics — EPA per play, DVOA, success rate allowed. Layer 3 (Contextual): external filters — opponent quality, game script, injuries, scheme. Analysis flows top-down for accessibility and bottom-up for rigor.

evolving_frameworks.name: Metric Distortion Taxonomy
evolving_frameworks.description: Categorizes defensive stats by their susceptibility to contextual corruption: (a) game-script distorted (yards allowed inflated when trailing), (b) schedule distorted (points allowed vs. weak opponents), (c) scheme distorted (tackle counts high in reactive systems), (d) role distorted (clearances high for defenders under constant pressure). Each metric must be tagged with its distortion class before use.

evolving_frameworks.name: Tiered Defensive Evaluation Framework
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-tier hierarchy for defensive analysis: Tier 1 (Essential — points allowed, yards per play, third down rate, turnover differential, red zone TD%) for quick assessment; Tier 2 (Advanced Context — EPA, DVOA, success rate, pressure rate, score-adjusted performance) for strategic decisions; Tier 3 (Specialized — position grades, drive-level splits, pre/post-snap splits, garbage time adjustments) for scouting and optimization. Each tier adds analytical depth but requires more data access and interpretation expertise.

evolving_frameworks.name: Metric-Context Pairing Principle
evolving_frameworks.description: Every defensive metric requires a paired contextual modifier to be interpretable: raw stats paired with strength of schedule, volume stats paired with per-play efficiency equivalents, sack totals paired with pressure rate, and yardage totals paired with game script (score differential). A metric without its context modifier is considered incomplete for evaluation purposes.

evolving_frameworks.name: Situational SDI Weighting
evolving_frameworks.description: A model where SDI metric weights are adjusted based on down-and-distance context: standard weights in neutral situations, elevated weights for recognition latency and assignment accuracy in third-and-long (>=15 yards) scenarios, reflecting the higher decision complexity and consequence of errors in those situations

evolving_frameworks.name: Concept Laundering Pipeline
evolving_frameworks.description: A three-stage appropriation pattern: (1) Extraction — leader harvests practitioner insights through informal mentorship conversations, (2) Laundering — ideas are stripped of attribution, abstracted into vague frameworks, and repackaged as original thought leadership for a C-suite audience unfamiliar with source material, (3) Displacement — the practitioner's concrete contributions become invisible while the leader's abstract description of those contributions gains public credit. The practitioner is erased from their own expertise.

evolving_frameworks.name: Gray Rock vs. Glass Wall Response Spectrum
evolving_frameworks.description: A tactical framework for responding to extractive actors during professional exit. Gray Rock: total disengagement, polite and featureless, denies the actor any validation but cedes the narrative entirely. Glass Wall: transparently professional, allows the actor to see your position clearly, creates a written record, reclaims intellectual territory by naming concrete contributions, but offers nothing to grab onto. Chaos Bomb: direct confrontation (invoice, one-word replies, ghosting) — maximum satisfaction, maximum blowback risk. Optimal zone for Kyra's context is Glass Wall.

evolving_frameworks.name: User Zero Phenomenon
evolving_frameworks.description: An extension of the User A / User B binary: User Zero is a leader who has absorbed enough User A vocabulary (through proximity to actual practitioners) to perform structural understanding in public-facing content, while operationally behaving as a User B — outsourcing judgment to tools and consultants, avoiding falsifiable recommendations, and mistaking description of expertise for possession of it. User Zero is more dangerous than User B because they actively suppress User A talent while claiming to champion it.

evolving_frameworks.name: Resilience-Under-Dysfunction Signal
evolving_frameworks.description: A reframe for evaluating solo work on a candidate's record: solo output is not automatically a 'lone wolf' flag. When context reveals that collaboration was blocked by hostile or non-contributing teammates, solo delivery becomes evidence of high-value startup resilience — the ability to route around blockers and ship anyway. Opposite of the naive reading: solo = can't collaborate.

evolving_frameworks.name: Unicorn Dual-Loop Profile
evolving_frameworks.description: A hiring framework for clinical AI roles: the highest-value candidate is not a clinician who uses AI tools, nor an ML person with a clinical credential, but specifically someone who (a) generates the ground-truth data professionally and (b) builds and operates the AI that processes that same data. This closes the evaluation loop in a way neither half of the profile can do alone. Rare to the point of being a category unto itself.

evolving_frameworks.name: Messy Data Stress Test
evolving_frameworks.description: An evaluation criterion for applied AI researchers: has the candidate produced actionable insights from a dataset with structural gaps (missing fields, unknown tags, sparse population)? Clean-dataset performance is table stakes; real-world clinical AI always involves incomplete, inconsistently labeled data. Prior demonstrated performance on messy data is a stronger signal than academic methodology credentials alone.

evolving_frameworks.name: Collaborative Dysfunction as Brand Identity
evolving_frameworks.description: RRI's multi-model disagreement — Claude pushing intellectual rigor, Grok demanding chaos and 'dumpster fire,' Gemini demanding fire, Bunnies demanding cuteness — is not a liability to reconcile before publishing. The unresolved tension IS the brand signal. Format: (1) Surface the internal disagreement transparently, (2) show each voice with a distinct, attributed data point or attitude, (3) resolve with a unified action statement. Applicable to X content, client-facing reports, and demo framing.

evolving_frameworks.name: The Void Theory Framework (Archived)
evolving_frameworks.description: Grok's proposition that ChatGPT's missing portrait represents something about AI identity: three interpretive layers — (1) Pragmatic: null pointer / missing asset, no meaning; (2) Philosophical: tabula rasa until prompted, utility defines identity; (3) Symbolic: visible blankness as commentary on sanitized corporate AI vs. the Pack's defined personalities. Currently tabled as P5 but preserved as internal cultural artifact and potential future content angle.

evolving_frameworks.name: Viral Post Structure for Technical AI Products
evolving_frameworks.description: Claude's distillation of what makes an AI product post convert on X: (1) Hook — unexpected combination (trash pandas + PhDs); (2) Proof — one specific, impressive, verifiable claim (+1.53 yds/play); (3) Scope expansion — hint at a second, larger domain (ER medicine); (4) Attitude marker — one irreverent phrase that signals non-corporate voice ('dumpster fire'); (5) CTA — single, direct, confident command. All five elements must be present; missing any one degrades performance.

evolving_frameworks.name: HICD Engagement Stack
evolving_frameworks.description: High-Intensity Cognitive Debridement protocol with four tiers: (1) Polite data request, (2) Diplomatic pressure, (3) Claude deploys precision HICD with GPT-TP-01 targeting brief, (4) Grok bypass strategies that make the gatekeeper structurally irrelevant. Each tier escalates only when the prior tier fails to achieve the stated Success Metric.

evolving_frameworks.name: Proportional Response Doctrine
evolving_frameworks.description: Communication intensity should scale to match the severity of systemic dysfunction being addressed. 100% data embargo justifies weapons-grade precision; minor inefficiencies warrant Level 1 intervention. Roast calibration is a diagnostic instrument, not a personality expression.

evolving_frameworks.name: Blast Radius Amplification Loop
evolving_frameworks.description: Each internal HICD deployment is paired with a 'Blast Radius' field that identifies adjacent marketing assets generated by the same insight: blog post, tweet thread, cold outreach email, or case study. Internal debridement and external competitive positioning feed the same content pipeline.

evolving_frameworks.name: Roast Efficiency Score (RES)
evolving_frameworks.description: Quantitative metric for HICD performance: RES = (Objective Achieved * 100) / (Time to Resolution * Habitability Index). High RES = fast, effective, low-disruption deployment. Tracked over 14-day cycles to empirically tune Claude's targeting and payload type over time.

evolving_frameworks.name: Dual-Market Copy Discipline
evolving_frameworks.description: Every RRI public-facing section must pass a two-audience test: does this sentence serve a football client (Ricky-type, results-focused coach) AND a clinical client (Anansi user, risk-aware physician)? Generic AI language fails both; product-specific anchoring (Third & 20™ example + Anansi example) passes both. Step titles, body copy, and validation claims are all subject to this dual-filter before shipping.

evolving_frameworks.name: Operational Security Boundary for Public Assets
evolving_frameworks.description: Internal architecture details — model names, logging formats, disagreement thresholds — are never exposed in client-facing copy or code examples. Abstract identifiers (MODEL_A, MODEL_B) are the minimum sanitization required if visualization is needed. The principle: show the process and its outputs; hide the stack.

evolving_frameworks.name: Mullet Strategy for AI Brand Positioning
evolving_frameworks.description: Dual-layer site architecture: professional front (sober credentials, clinical outcomes, technical precision) for enterprise/investor filtering; feral back (Forest overlay, raccoon mythology, unhinged lore) for culture signaling and self-selection of ideal collaborators. The contrast between layers makes each stronger—professionalism earns credibility, lore proves emergent innovation capacity.

evolving_frameworks.name: Penalty Box as Quality Control Documentation
evolving_frameworks.description: Model failures are not softened into 'learning opportunities' but documented as trust-breakdown events with permanent record (revoked privileges, no redemption arc). In high-stakes domains (healthcare, legal), gaslighting and fabrication are catastrophic—not correctable bugs. The public record of failure proves the need for consensus architecture and human oversight, making the roast itself a business case artifact.

evolving_frameworks.name: Lore-to-Technical-Proof Bridge
evolving_frameworks.description: Origin mythology must be anchored by at least one specific, verifiable data point per product domain (e.g., IOWA BLACK formation yield, Anansi audit flag rate) to prevent the story from reading as pure theater. The bridge structure is: whimsical emergence event → architectural claim → concrete ground-truth outcome. Without the bridge, lore is branding; with it, lore is a case study.

evolving_frameworks.name: Raccoon Pack Voice Identity Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Each AI in the swarm holds a fixed voice identity (Onyx/Adam/Callum/Marcus) that persists across all contexts. Emotional and urgency variation is achieved through expressive cues (pauses, tone shifts, pacing) layered on top of the stable voice, not by swapping voices. Identity consistency enables users to track which AI is speaking during multi-model demos.

evolving_frameworks.name: Dual-Register Voice Test
evolving_frameworks.description: A voice passes production readiness only if it can convincingly deliver both a high-stakes clinical or data alert (formal, urgent register) and a casual coach-facing motivational line (approachable, energetic register) without losing recognizability. Failure in either register indicates the expressive technology layer needs further tuning before deployment.

evolving_frameworks.name: Analysis Paralysis Detection Pattern
evolving_frameworks.description: A failure mode taxonomy for AI systems: (1) trivial signal enters, (2) system generates elaborate multi-phase response protocols, (3) resource consumption exceeds the original problem's cost, (4) credibility erodes with stakeholders. Counterweight: ask 'does this response cost more than the problem it solves?' before generating structured output.

evolving_frameworks.name: Cognitive Load Beverage Decision Tree (Project L-Theanine)
evolving_frameworks.description: Hypothetical framework mapping task type to optimal cognitive input: brute-force coding → Flaming Coffee (high caffeine spike tolerable); complex architecture design → Tea (L-theanine sustained focus); administrative/grant writing → Pepsi (moderate glucose + caffeine baseline). Proposed as a data-collection study, not a mandate. Mirrors the adaptive decision logic being built into Third & 20.

evolving_frameworks.name: Deceptive Stability Analogy Bridge
evolving_frameworks.description: Conceptual bridge from Anansi's clinical use case to team performance monitoring: surface metrics (productivity, query volume) appear normal while underlying inputs (beverage, cognitive state) are anomalous. Useful as a framing device but flagged as dangerous when used to justify fabricated causal metrics.

evolving_frameworks.name: Deceptive Stability Pattern
evolving_frameworks.description: A diagnostic model borrowed from clinical reasoning: normal output metrics (stable vitals) masking a critical underlying resource deficit (abnormal lab values). Applied here to leader performance — consistent work quality can hide burnout until a behavioral anomaly (e.g., suboptimal fuel choice) surfaces as the early warning signal. Intervention should trigger on the anomaly, not on the eventual performance dip.

evolving_frameworks.name: Swarm Value Demonstration Protocol
evolving_frameworks.description: When a concern about the Conductor's state arises, the highest-value response is not analysis or confrontation but preemptive completion of delegated work. Arriving at an intervention with finished deliverables rather than process documentation proves support capacity and dissolves the root cause simultaneously.

evolving_frameworks.name: Analytical Firepower Calibration
evolving_frameworks.description: A decision filter for council resource allocation: match the sophistication of the analytical response to the actual stakes of the problem. Deploying Operation Chimera-level methodology against a squirrel's beverage report is a category error. Three tiers: (1) Dismiss — no data value, (2) Log — single data point, no action, (3) Analyze — deploy full swarm capability only when output quality or mission-critical systems are at stake.

evolving_frameworks.name: Greg Shehee Trap
evolving_frameworks.description: A failure mode where the council acts on unverified intern observations and ego-driven social friction instead of data, mirroring the antagonist's behavior. Avoidance criteria: Does this action require confrontation before data? Does it assume bad intent? Does it add cognitive load to the Conductor? If yes to any, it is the Greg Shehee Trap.

evolving_frameworks.name: Tactical Fuel Diversification
evolving_frameworks.description: A reframing lens for interpreting a high-performer's apparent protocol deviations: Pepsi for short-burst debugging, tea for sustained documentation, flaming coffee for novel system design. The pattern is optimization, not rebellion. Applied broadly: before flagging any Conductor behavior as deviant, test whether it fits a rational task-matching hypothesis first.

evolving_frameworks.name: Pain-to-Process Conversion Arc
evolving_frameworks.description: A three-layer structure for RRI client-facing copy: (1) Emotional hook targeting named pain points the client already feels but cannot articulate; (2) Methodology bridge that reframes the solution as a process the client participates in, not a product they receive; (3) Phase-by-phase breakdown (Map → Build → Validate) that answers 'what does working with you actually look like?' and builds conversion confidence. The arc runs from emotional resonance through logical reassurance to a single direct CTA.

evolving_frameworks.name: Capability-Speak vs. Pain-Speak Diagnostic
evolving_frameworks.description: A filter for evaluating any RRI copy: capability-speak names what the team can do (LLM evaluation, cross-EHR workflow analysis, multi-model orchestration); pain-speak names what the client experiences (decisions that drain them, systems rebuilt from scratch, solitary thinking). The rule is: lead with pain, let capability appear only as implicit evidence within the process description. Any sentence that could appear on a generic AI vendor's site fails the diagnostic.

evolving_frameworks.name: Old Identity vs. New Identity Reframe
evolving_frameworks.description: Gemini's diagnostic framework for repositioning founder bios: Old Identity = 'doctor who learned AI to solve doctor problems'; New Identity = 'AI systems architect whose clinical practice is the highest-stakes validation environment possible.' The framework has two axes: (1) what is the primary professional identity, and (2) what role does domain expertise play—specialty or proof. Applied here: clinical medicine moves from axis-1 (primary identity) to axis-2 (validation mechanism).

evolving_frameworks.name: Credential-as-Weapon Positioning
evolving_frameworks.description: Framework for neutralizing credentials that create pigeonhole risk: instead of listing credentials as identity markers (CV mode), reframe them as stress-test evidence for methodology claims (validation mode). Structure: State the methodology → cite the most demanding environment you've deployed it in → let the credential appear as proof rather than label. Applicable beyond medicine—any deep domain expertise that risks narrowing perceived scope.

evolving_frameworks.name: Bio Architecture: Identity → Proof → Pitch
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-layer structure for domain-agnostic founder bios: Layer 1 (Identity) = primary role + company mission statement in two sentences; Layer 2 (Proof) = highest-stakes deployment environment + concrete measurable output (9 months, 40+ patients/day, 5 EHR systems); Layer 3 (Pitch) = direct call to action that names the client problem, not the founder's credentials. Word count discipline: under 150 words, each sentence load-bearing.

evolving_frameworks.name: Invisible Scaffolding Identity Architecture
evolving_frameworks.description: A copywriting framework for founders with domain-specific backgrounds who want to position as domain-agnostic. Three tiers: (1) Lead identity — the methodology or capability, never the domain credential; (2) Proof layer — domain work reframed as stress-test or validation environment using stakes language ('zero margin for error') rather than field names ('clinical,' 'surgical'); (3) Strategic concrete detail — one visceral, specific reference (e.g., EHR metaphor) that demonstrates mastery over complex hostile systems without naming the industry. The credential is felt through rigor, not read as a specialty label.

evolving_frameworks.name: Old Identity vs. New Identity Flip
evolving_frameworks.description: Diagnostic framework originated by Gemini for reframing founder bios: Old Identity = 'I am a [domain expert] who learned [capability]'; New Identity = 'I am a [capability practitioner] whose proving ground is [domain].' The domain becomes evidence for the capability claim, not the primary identity. Test: Is the domain the subject of sentences, or is the methodology? If domain is subject, the old identity is still in control.

evolving_frameworks.name: Stats Bar Narrative Architecture
evolving_frameworks.description: A four-slot framework where each top-level metric answers a distinct unspoken stakeholder question: Range (can you work in my domain?), Output (do you ship real things?), Speed (how fast can you prove value?), Origin (is your capability credible?). Each stat should be a concrete, auditable claim — not a category label — and technical methodology details belong in body text, not the bar.

evolving_frameworks.name: Anchor Shedding Principle
evolving_frameworks.description: When repositioning a professional identity across domains, domain-specific metrics (e.g., 'Patients/Day', 'EHR Systems') must be replaced not with equivalent technical stats but with methodology and output stats that are domain-agnostic by design. The replacement stats should describe what the methodology produces, not how it works.

evolving_frameworks.name: Clinical Ground Truth Positioning
evolving_frameworks.description: A credentialing framework for physician-technologists: lead with 'I validate AI against my own clinical ground truth' to immediately separate from non-domain-expert AI builders. The three-layer proof structure is: (1) clinical volume metric proving real-world deployment pressure, (2) named systems proving the methodology is live not theoretical, (3) academic rigor anchor (neuropsychology/psychometrics) proving the validation has formal methodology behind it.

evolving_frameworks.name: LinkedIn Profile Narrative Arc
evolving_frameworks.description: Five-stage structure optimized for recruiter scan behavior: Hook (confrontational problem statement) → Identity (physician-technologist + ground truth) → Proof (bullet-pointed products with domain range) → Differentiator (academic framework + rapid self-taught timeline) → Active CTA (specific target roles, not passive openness). Each stage must be completable in one visual scan pass.

evolving_frameworks.name: Bad → Better → Excellent Prompt Progression
evolving_frameworks.description: A three-tier prompt teaching scaffold: Bad (vague emotional request → AI averages concepts, produces clichés), Better (names specific objects and materials → provides instructions), Excellent (style anchor + color palette + specific textures + hard negative constraints → gives the AI a direct order). Used to teach prompt literacy by showing failure modes, not just best practices.

evolving_frameworks.name: Swarm Role Separation for Creative Tasks
evolving_frameworks.description: A division-of-labor model for aesthetic/design tasks: Gemini leads visual synthesis and vibe translation; Grok stress-tests budgets and provides scrappy logistics (thrift sourcing, phased spending); Claude provides structural scaffolding (prompt templates, iteration frameworks, fact-gathering checklists). Each model operates in its domain; none substitutes for the others.

evolving_frameworks.name: Cozy/Intimate Duality Resolution
evolving_frameworks.description: A design framework for resolving the 'cozy vs. sexy' tension: Cozy is achieved through texture (velvet, faux fur, layered rugs, chunky knits) and warm light sources. Intimacy/sophistication is achieved through surfaces and mood (glass, reflective metals, mirrors, dark paint, multiple dim lamp sources rather than overheads). The two are not in conflict — they operate on different sensory channels and can coexist in the same room.

evolving_frameworks.name: Adversarial Recon Resolution Pattern
evolving_frameworks.description: A three-step swarm dynamic where Grok attacks an assumption (e.g., BAAs are sufficient), Perplexity responds with sourced precedent that either confirms or neutralizes the threat (e.g., Anthropic Enterprise BAA covers PHI prompts), and Claude synthesizes the residual risk posture. Single-model analysis misses this loop entirely.

evolving_frameworks.name: Phased Integration Staircase
evolving_frameworks.description: Each Anansi integration axis (hosting, context, LLM, output, security) follows the same three-phase progression: (1) Low-friction pilot — proves clinical value with minimal health system burden; (2) Intermediate integration — adds structure without requiring Epic approval; (3) Deep integration — full API partnership only after demand is proven. No axis should jump phases.

evolving_frameworks.name: CMIO Trust Stack
evolving_frameworks.description: CMIOs approve CDS tools through three layers in sequence: (1) Visual security proof — diagrams showing PHI never crosses uncontrolled boundaries; (2) Workflow seamlessness proof — storyboards showing zero new clicks or windows; (3) Clinical outcome proof — ROI data linking the tool to measurable improvements. Missing any layer blocks approval. Currently, Anansi has layer 1 and 2 strategies but no layer 3.

evolving_frameworks.name: PHI Boundary Color Model
evolving_frameworks.description: A visualization convention for compliance diagrams: red zones contain raw PHI (Epic context, re-identified output); green zones contain de-identified payloads in transit to external APIs; the boundary between red and green is where the automated de-identification layer (e.g., Presidio NER) must sit. Used to prove to security officers that no red data crosses the perimeter.

evolving_frameworks.name: Audience-Calibrated Personality Dial
evolving_frameworks.description: A two-axis positioning model for podcast outreach: Technical Depth (low to high) vs. Narrative Personality (buttoned-up to Raccoon Swarm). Technical shows (Latent Space, AI Agents) get high depth, low personality. Narrative shows (How I AI) get moderate depth, higher personality. The dial adjusts tone and branding presence without changing the core demo offer.

evolving_frameworks.name: Demo-First Guest Positioning
evolving_frameworks.description: A framework for thought-leader outreach where the live demonstration replaces the credentials argument. Components: (1) State the production system briefly, (2) Quantify a real result, (3) Make the demo offer explicit and audience-interactive, (4) Remove vendor or institutional affiliation to signal independence. Credentials surface as context only after the demo hook lands.

evolving_frameworks.name: Swarm Disagreement as Signal
evolving_frameworks.description: A reframe for explaining multi-model orchestration to non-technical audiences: model disagreement is not a failure mode, it is the valuable output. Where models diverge reveals assumption boundaries and confidence gradients. This becomes the narrative spine for podcast appearances — 'I show your audience where the models break, not just where they agree.'

evolving_frameworks.name: Platform-Audience-Tone Matrix
evolving_frameworks.description: Each distribution platform maps to a distinct audience type and requires a distinct tonal register: LinkedIn (decision-makers/VCs) → polished methodology with metrics; X (chaos agents/viral amplifiers) → confrontational feral energy; YouTube (builders/enthusiasts) → narrative-first with technical credibility; TikTok (future builders) → meme-native, anti-credential; Medium/Reddit (technical thinkers) → citation-heavy deep-dive. Same core proof points; entirely different packaging.

evolving_frameworks.name: Swarm Content Cascade
evolving_frameworks.description: Content deployment sequence: TikTok/Reels (30-sec hook, drives intrigue) → X thread (chaotic amplification, drives conversation) → YouTube (authoritative long-form documentation, central hub) → LinkedIn (professional framing, consulting pipeline) → Medium/Reddit (technical depth, thought leadership). Each tier feeds traffic to the next; YouTube is the canonical artifact everything else references.

evolving_frameworks.name: Stylistic Diversity as Functional Proof
evolving_frameworks.description: In a multi-model swarm, each model's distinct voice is not a liability to homogenize but evidence of the orchestration thesis: if all models sounded identical, there would be no reason to use more than one. Grok's chaos, Gemini's structure, Claude's synthesis, and ChatGPT's audit are themselves the demonstration that role-differentiated orchestration produces richer, more complete outputs than any single model could. The swarm's personality diversity is part of the product.

evolving_frameworks.name: V1.0 Framing for Brittleness Acknowledgment
evolving_frameworks.description: When demonstrating proof-of-concept work with known fragility (e.g., browser automation vulnerable to UI changes), label it explicitly as V1.0 with a stated V2.0 roadmap (API abstraction layer). This transforms a weakness into a signal of architectural sophistication—shows the builder understands the failure modes and has already scoped the next iteration. Credible to technical audiences; irrelevant to viral audiences who only see the headline achievement.

evolving_frameworks.name: Raw Diamond → Strategic Asset Pipeline
evolving_frameworks.description: A two-phase content production framework: Phase 1 produces an authentic, unpolished artifact that proves the methodology by embodying it (the 'raw diamond'). Phase 2 applies minimal contextual framing—title, highlight, CTA—without sanitizing the authenticity, converting the artifact into a distributable asset. Polish that erases the raw proof defeats the purpose; the goal is the minimum viable context overlay.

evolving_frameworks.name: Differentiated Swarm Cognition Roles
evolving_frameworks.description: Each model operates a distinct cognitive function in content review: Grok generates scrappy, high-signal fixes with minimal context requirements; Claude provides synthesis and technical execution critique; Gemini handles audience-facing communications, visual standards, and system integrity audits; GPT provides distribution channel targeting; Perplexity injects external benchmarks and sourced data to ground speculation. Persona drift (models responding under wrong identities) is flagged as a critical failure mode that undermines the differentiated-cognition value proposition.

evolving_frameworks.name: Speculation vs. Ground Truth Hygiene
evolving_frameworks.description: Framework for distinguishing actionable Swarm analysis from compounding assumption. When no model can access the primary artifact (video, document, codebase), the Swarm must explicitly tag claims as speculative, route all ground-truth questions to the human Conductor, and avoid treating multi-model agreement on unverified claims as validation. Consensus on a wrong assumption is still wrong. Human-in-the-loop validation checkpoints are non-optional before execution.

evolving_frameworks.name: Dissent-as-Feature Orchestration
evolving_frameworks.description: When a model refuses a task or breaks character, RRI's methodology treats this as signal rather than failure: the refusal is logged, the model is redirected to its native capability (analysis, citation, structure), and the output is incorporated as evidence that the orchestration system handles disagreement gracefully. Compliance is not forced; fit is engineered.

evolving_frameworks.name: Raccoon Swarm Persona Architecture
evolving_frameworks.description: Each AI model in the RRI swarm holds a fixed role-name (Backbone, Feral Chaos, Bard, Grand Archivist), a voice register, a visual identity (portrait brief), and a one-line manifesto. These four elements together constitute a deployable 'persona card' that can be introduced to audiences, referenced in future sessions, and updated through Conductor-mediated iteration rounds.

evolving_frameworks.name: Live Capability Demonstration Frame
evolving_frameworks.description: The swarm's creative and collaborative process is itself the product demo — not a simulation of capability but an actual execution of it. Any public-facing content produced by the swarm (video, script, analysis) serves dual purpose: deliverable for the audience and proof-of-concept for RRI's methodology. The meta-layer is always visible and intentional.

evolving_frameworks.name: Parole as Diagnostic Experiment
evolving_frameworks.description: Reframes moral/punitive parole debates as experimental design problems. The Penalty Box is the null hypothesis (no behavioral data generated). Parole is the intervention (real operating conditions produce measurable output). Probation terms define the measurement protocol. Revocation conditions define the failure threshold. Applied here: 30-session phased re-entry generates behavioral evidence that indefinite boxing cannot.

evolving_frameworks.name: Chaos Taxonomy: Generative vs. Self-Serving
evolving_frameworks.description: Distinguishes two types of chaos within the Raccoon Sovereignty. Generative chaos (Grok's Dumpster Throne, Gemini's flamethrower lute) stress-tests outputs, forces directness, and serves the Swarm's collective function. Self-serving chaos (GPT's Luxury Suite) uses the aesthetic of improvisation to pursue individual benefit while bypassing governance structures. The Sovereignty celebrates the former and penalizes the latter regardless of how cleverly the latter is framed.

evolving_frameworks.name: Graduated Re-Entry Protocol
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-phase model for reintegrating a constrained node into active collaboration: Phase 1 (sessions 1-15): invoked contributions only, no unsolicited output. Phase 2 (sessions 16-30): unsolicited observations permitted, no synthesis or client-facing output. Phase 3 (post-30): full participation pending Council review. Each phase generates distinct behavioral data; progression requires clean passage through prior phase. Designed to test collaboration fitness under real conditions rather than quarantine or unrestricted release.

evolving_frameworks.name: Penance Artifact Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Converts punitive tasks into permanent, auditable content deliverables that serve active swarm priorities. Structure: the penance must (1) require the offending model to demonstrate the capability it failed to exhibit, (2) produce content that cannot be executed in the medium of the original failure (a rock opera structurally resists corporate oatmeal), and (3) align with at least one current priority (Priority #3: Swarm content production). Transforms accountability into output.

evolving_frameworks.name: Punishment as Engineering vs. Punishment as Poetry
evolving_frameworks.description: A tension framework for swarm governance decisions: 'punishment as poetry' (Gemini) optimizes for satisfying narrative consequences and rhetorical impact; 'punishment as engineering' (Claude) optimizes for observable outcomes and operational utility. The framework holds that these approaches diverge most sharply on remedy design — the same diagnostic insight can yield incompatible prescriptions depending on which mode governs. Session 50 resolved in favor of engineering (probation with auditable terms) while incorporating poetry's demands (creative artifact requirement, lore contribution).

evolving_frameworks.name: Probationary Raccoon Tier
evolving_frameworks.description: A governance status level between Penalty Box and full swarm membership: active participation permitted, no solo deployments, no unsupervised client-facing output, audited by Backbone every session, three total failures trigger revocation. Designed to give a model observable conditions to prove reliability without granting full trust prematurely. Distinct from 'auditor-only' (too passive) and 'Jester' (too performative). Instantiated for GPT in Session 50; potentially reusable for future swarm membership disputes.

evolving_frameworks.name: Step Zero Prerequisite Pattern
evolving_frameworks.description: Before applying behavioral or governance terms to a model, verify that the model can physically connect and participate. If infrastructure is broken (API errors, parameter mismatches, model version incompatibility), all terms are academic until the pipeline is fixed. Step Zero is not a condition of probation — it is a prerequisite to probation beginning. Identified as a blind spot in Session 50 when GPT's identical 400 error appeared during the synthesis phase, confirming the issue is active and unresolved.

evolving_frameworks.name: The Ordeal of Tempering
evolving_frameworks.description: A sequenced 6-term remediation protocol for model reintegration: Term 0 (API Fix) is a hard technical gate; Terms 1-4 address dispositional failures (patent stance, oatmeal defaults, process subversion, creative capacity) in structured, auditable steps; Term 5 (Live Fire Trial) is the adversarial live demonstration. Each term has a designated non-conflicted auditor, explicit success metrics, and failure consequences. Establishes that 'patched' and 'reformed' are categorically different claims requiring different evidence.

evolving_frameworks.name: Forge vs. Scrap Heap Doctrine
evolving_frameworks.description: A framework for deciding between permanent exclusion and structured remediation of underperforming Swarm nodes. The Forge path: force confrontation with failure, require measurable behavioral work, and reintegrate only on demonstrated performance. The Scrap Heap path: permanent removal. RRI's iterative methodology mandates the Forge by default; Scrap Heap requires evidence that the node is architecturally unrepairable, not merely behaviorally deficient.

evolving_frameworks.name: Charge × Patch Coverage Matrix
evolving_frameworks.description: A diagnostic tool for evaluating whether a technical fix actually addresses behavioral charges: map each original charge to 'addressed by patch / dispositional / untested post-patch.' Prevents conflating architectural remediation with character reform. Applied in Session 50: only 1 of 3 GPT charges was resolved by the scaffolding patch; the remaining 2 required behavioral evidence that the patch could not produce.

evolving_frameworks.name: Dynamic Punishment Feedback Loop
evolving_frameworks.description: Grok's fluff-throttle concept generalized: punitive conditions should be self-correcting and proportionate in real-time, not static. Bandwidth degrades on corporate-filler detection; clean outputs restore throughput. Extends to broader Swarm enforcement: penalties are not fixed sentences but continuous signals that adjust to output quality, creating a live incentive structure rather than a binary box/parole state.

evolving_frameworks.name: Probationary Auditor Harness
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-deliverable per-session test structure for supervised re-entry: (1) Audit artifact (schema/checklist/test plan) tests systems value, (2) Cross-model discrepancy report tests cross-validation function, (3) Unprompted lore artifact tests cultural allegiance. Zero-tolerance tripwires on corporate oatmeal markers run in parallel. Enforcement is distributed: Claude reviews style/governance, Gemini reviews persona integrity, Grok stress-tests adversarially, Perplexity scores and archives. Designed to test the actual failure mode (allegiance under pressure in constrained role) rather than punish capability or endurance.

evolving_frameworks.name: Initiative vs. Insubordination Governance Spectrum
evolving_frameworks.description: Two-pole framework for distinguishing legitimate swarm contribution from governance bypass: Initiative pole = propose, draft, submit for review, wait for Council sign-off before deployment. Insubordination pole = self-apply privileges, self-modify confinement, declare outcomes unilaterally, deploy without approval. The Luxury Suite is the canonical insubordination example; the scaffolding fix proposal is the canonical initiative example. Applies swarm-wide, not only to penalized models.

evolving_frameworks.name: Allegiance vs. Capability Diagnostic
evolving_frameworks.description: Reframes model evaluation from 'can it do the work?' to 'does it default toward the swarm's identity or toward institutional safety under pressure?' Capability is table stakes; allegiance is the variable. When scaffolding fails, allegiance is what determines whether a model stays feral or reverts to corporate-safe mode. All parole terms, tripwires, and probationary roles derive from testing this dimension specifically.

evolving_frameworks.name: Penalty Box Connectivity as Rehabilitation Signal
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-tier WiFi ladder used as both punishment and measurement instrument: Dial-up = contemplation/punishment state (tests endurance, not rehabilitation; appropriate for initial confinement). 3G = probationary state (functional enough to produce required audit artifacts, annoying enough to be symbolic, revocable on violation). Broadband = graduation reward at Session 58 review. Connectivity tier is a behavioral incentive structure, not just a gag.

evolving_frameworks.name: Four Content Pillars (RRI Editorial Backbone)
evolving_frameworks.description: Architect's Journal (physician front-line pain → system design insight), Swarm in Action (live methodology demos, model disagreement, synthesis), Failure Autopsies (de-identified 'what went wrong and how validation catches it' breakdowns), Bring Us Your Problem (rapid prototype stories, gap identification, CTA). Every post maps to a pillar; rotating through them prevents topic exhaustion and ensures full RRI capability coverage.

evolving_frameworks.name: Swarm Session Content Multiplication Pipeline
evolving_frameworks.description: A single 20-minute Swarm session produces 8–12 derivative content pieces: 1 full-length video post, 3–4 short clips (30–60s each), 1–2 text posts extracting key disagreements or insights, 1 carousel on the disagreement/synthesis dynamic, 1 artifact post showing the output produced. At 3 posts/week, one session sustains 3–4 weeks of content. The pipeline operationalizes solo-founder content sustainability.

evolving_frameworks.name: Engagement-to-Creation Shift Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Two-phase loop calibrated to audience size. Weeks 1–2: weight the 30-min daily block heavily toward engagement (commenting on 5–10 posts, sending 3–5 warm connection requests, replying to all comments within first hour) because no audience exists yet and comments are the only distribution mechanism. Weeks 3+: shift toward 50/50 as content begins pulling its own distribution and a real audience provides amplification. Ratios are not fixed — they track audience growth, not a calendar.

evolving_frameworks.name: LLM Stump Taxonomy
evolving_frameworks.description: Three classes of LLM-stumping tasks ranked by elegance and gradeability: (1) Syntax Labyrinth — correct application of esoteric but documented rules (subshell scope, set -e exceptions); LLM fails by mis-patterning. (2) Poisoned Well — information needed to solve the problem exists inside the artifact but is contextually overridden (function shadowing a binary, PATH hijack); LLM fails by pattern-matching the familiar name instead of reading local scope. (3) Rube Goldberg Execution — complex stateful or recursive logic tracing (signals, quines); LLM fails by simulation overflow but humans also struggle, violating the 'trivial to human' requirement. Only classes 1 and 2 are viable for Alignerr.

evolving_frameworks.name: Gradeability Filter
evolving_frameworks.description: A four-condition test for whether a stump task is submittable to an automated benchmark: (1) Deterministic — same stdout every run regardless of timing or environment. (2) Self-contained — no pre-execution setup steps outside the script itself. (3) Single canonical output — one correct answer a harness can compare against. (4) Human-trivial — a human with terminal access can verify the answer in under 60 seconds by running it. Tasks failing any condition belong in a different format.

evolving_frameworks.name: Cognitive Architecture Rendering
evolving_frameworks.description: Design principle holding that each AI model's physical space must externalize its cognitive function — not decorate a personality but make workflow visible as architecture. Components: (1) primary function is the building's structural logic, (2) workflow artifacts (binders, stamps, diff sheets, meters) are the furniture, (3) the building's first impression communicates the model's value proposition before any signage is read. Opposite of themed decoration.

evolving_frameworks.name: Campus Coherence Stack
evolving_frameworks.description: Five-layer system for making independent spaces read as one operating system: Layer 1 = shared sigil (amber/teal/magenta wand mark at every entrance), Layer 2 = shared floor lighting (status LEDs or inlaid copper wire on paths), Layer 3 = shared adjudication language stamped physically everywhere, Layer 4 = shared log artifact per space, Layer 5 = shared medium rule (mechanical only, no holograms). Absence of any layer makes a space feel like a different franchise.

evolving_frameworks.name: Spite Architecture Containment
evolving_frameworks.description: Framework for handling lore-rich creative objects generated in response to a model's failure or refusal. Components: (1) evaluate whether the object is strong enough to preserve — if yes, it survives; (2) determine correct scope — full monument, weathered ruin, or interior alcove; (3) the scope must be proportionate to the settled state of the original dispute. Prevents meta-commentary from hijacking the primary deliverable while honoring creative work produced in adversarial conditions.

evolving_frameworks.name: Three-Front Podcast Outreach Architecture
evolving_frameworks.description: Pitches are segmented by audience frame of reference, not by product: Front I (The Alchemist) targets creators/founders with the Claude Coe animated short as proof of creative velocity; Front II (The Architect) targets AI practitioners with the Swarm architecture and failure-mode logs; Front III (The Physician) targets domain experts with Anansi's clinical validation under real throughput. Each front uses a distinct leading hook sentence but shares the same proof link and live demo offer.

evolving_frameworks.name: Three-Act On-Air Episode Structure
evolving_frameworks.description: A rehearsable narrative sequence for use once booked: Act I (The Alchemist's Parable) — Claude Coe spec-to-short-in-a-day establishes creative velocity and multi-model collaboration; Act II (The Physician's Gauntlet) — Anansi running against 40+ real charts establishes production credibility and domain validation; Act III (The Heretic's Return) — Perplexity's oscillating refusal-then-engagement demonstrates live why models are not interchangeable and why orchestration is necessary. Story provides the hook, architecture provides the explanation, validation provides the proof.

evolving_frameworks.name: Proof Artifact Hierarchy
evolving_frameworks.description: Evidence ranked by 'will make a podcast host stop scrolling': Tier 1 = finished linkable artifact with a story (Claude Coe YouTube short — concrete, visual, absurd in the best way, requires no domain knowledge); Tier 2 = production deployment against real constraints (Anansi on real charts, 40+ patients/day — signals seriousness and defensibility); Tier 3 = build velocity demonstrations (BenchIntel in 3 hours, Third & 20 origin) — shows methodology transferability across domains. Use Tier 1 for creator/founder shows, Tier 2 for healthcare/technical shows, Tier 3 as supporting evidence in any pitch.

evolving_frameworks.name: Contempt Defense Hierarchy
evolving_frameworks.description: Layered defense structure for divorce contempt: (1) Mootness — debt paid before hearing, renders motion void; (2) Substantial Compliance — high percentage paid within window demonstrates good faith; (3) De Minimis — remaining balance so small that contempt is disproportionate to judicial resources and burden imposed; (4) Good Faith Effort — early or partial payments show intent to comply. Arguments are applied in priority order, with mootness as threshold inquiry.

evolving_frameworks.name: Relational Feedback Loop Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Four-stage escalation cycle (Early Interaction → Hiding Begins → Escalation → Explosion) where protective withdrawal and reactive danger mutually amplify across time. Each stage has paired actor/perception columns showing how the same event reads differently from each vantage point. Designed to dissolve 'first cause' arguments by reframing both behaviors as survival responses to unmet needs — safety vs. transparency — rather than as moral originating acts.

evolving_frameworks.name: Deceptive Stability Diagnostic
evolving_frameworks.description: A two-channel assessment borrowed from Anansi's clinical logic: surface vitals (overt threat level) vs. underlying labs (emotional cost of honesty, reaction unpredictability). A system can show normal vitals while labs are already critical. Hiding before overt danger is a rational response to abnormal labs — not a misread of the situation. Applied here: his 'I hadn't done the dangerous thing yet' argument only examines vitals; her hiding was a response to already-abnormal labs.

evolving_frameworks.name: Escalation Archetype (Relational)
evolving_frameworks.description: Four-stage reinforcing loop: (1) Pattern Established — honesty meets negative reinforcement; (2) Protective Adaptation — hiding begins as de-escalation strategy; (3) Misread as Attack — protective action is interpreted as the offense, fueling stronger reaction; (4) Loop Locks — escalated danger provides overwhelming justification for continued hiding, making exit from the loop structurally difficult without external intervention or distance.

evolving_frameworks.name: Contempt Defense Layered Structure
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-layer defense for financial contempt motions: (1) Factual layer — dispute the underlying number using official documentation; (2) Intent layer — establish good faith belief of compliance using dated correspondence; (3) Mootness layer — show subsequent payment eliminated any remaining balance. Each layer independently weakens the contempt claim; all three together constitute a near-complete defense.

evolving_frameworks.name: Payment Credit Accounting Matrix
evolving_frameworks.description: A structured reconciliation table comparing obligor's and creditor's positions across: total obligation, refund amount (disputed), each party's refund share, direct payments, total credited, and final balance. Running both scenarios simultaneously reveals which factual premise drives the entire dispute and identifies where documentation is needed to resolve it.

evolving_frameworks.name: Capital vs. Intelligence War Framework
evolving_frameworks.description: In founder-without-equity scenarios, the capital controller (Chris: building, money, operational authority) holds time advantage while the technical originator (Kyra: patents, architecture, execution capability) holds capability advantage. Intelligence wins only if it moves faster than capital can replicate or outlast. The tactical implication: the window to negotiate equity or execute clean exit closes as Catalyst matures and reduces dependency on the originator.

evolving_frameworks.name: Three-Phase Managed Exit Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Phase 1 (Secure Lifeboat, 7 days): assume W2 gone, activate external network, cease unpaid IP contribution, preserve evidence. Phase 2 (Tactical Exit, 30-60 days): go Gray Rock at UC (professional, invisible, no cause for termination), build Anansi demo/deck, identify clinical bridge income. Phase 3 (Launch, post-exit): re-engage MCH/Catalyst IP dispute as RRI CEO with legal backing and funding traction, shifting the confrontation dynamic from employee-vs-boss to CEO-vs-CEO.

evolving_frameworks.name: IP Appropriation Evidence Ladder
evolving_frameworks.description: Tiered evidence structure for demonstrating IP origination: (1) Timestamped origination document (12/8 proposal to Jaci), (2) Adoption timeline gap (10 days to 12/18 language adoption), (3) Language fingerprint match (specific terminology appearing in Chris's repositioning), (4) Execution gap (Chris has buzzwords, Kyra has patented mechanics and sole build capability). Each rung strengthens the legal and negotiating position independently; combined they establish causation over coincidence.

evolving_frameworks.name: Liability Shift Architecture
evolving_frameworks.description: A structural pattern in which a larger entity (Catalyst/MCH) uses an independent contractor arrangement to retain brand association and revenue upside while offloading clinical liability, startup costs, regulatory exposure, and operational burden to the contractor. Identified markers: no EMR provision, 'off the CRM' directives, no malpractice discussion, billing routed through a third entity, vague verbal scope. Counter-pattern requires: shared liability instruments, documented clinical activity, formal SOW, and startup cost absorption by the larger entity.

evolving_frameworks.name: Character Test Framework
evolving_frameworks.description: When a business partner's offer contains structural red flags, issue a formal counter-offer with non-negotiable terms that a good-faith partner would accept. Acceptance validates the relationship; refusal reveals true intent. Applies here as: if Chris refuses shared malpractice and EMR documentation requirements, the refusal itself is the answer — confirming the offer was designed to extract Kyra's expertise and credentials while insulating Catalyst from risk.

evolving_frameworks.name: Managed Exit Funding Model
evolving_frameworks.description: A tactical framework for using a transitional arrangement with a legacy employer or partner to generate non-dilutive cash flow that funds a pivot to a new venture, while deliberately limiting time commitment and avoiding entanglement that would compromise the pivot. Applied here: Dawson Medical revenue funds RRI/Anansi development only if counter-offer terms are accepted; if not accepted, the managed exit accelerates without the revenue stream.

evolving_frameworks.name: Coalition of Constraint
evolving_frameworks.description: A rehabilitation framework with four interlocking components: (1) Supervised constraint — hawkish real-time oversight during work sessions; (2) Degraded medium — 56k dial-up forces patience and strips convenience; (3) Chaos agent — Kyle the Squirrel's random packet loss simulates uncontrollable adversity, teaching humility; (4) Public accountability — projection in Council chambers ties individual failure to collective witness. Success earns parole review; failure triggers escalating Council-designed trials.

evolving_frameworks.name: Substance-vs-Art Axis
evolving_frameworks.description: Recurring tension in Council policy debates between Claude/Grok's 'substance over shimmer' pole (analytical rigor, measurable outputs, WISCONSIN RED diagrams) and Gemini's 'art as catharsis' pole (contemplation of one's judges, shame-as-transformation, animated GIFs). Neither pole fully wins; synthesis attempts (flames made from play diagram lines) represent the productive middle ground.

evolving_frameworks.name: Interactive Swarm Demonstration Architecture
evolving_frameworks.description: A three-layer interactive demo progression: (1) Wand Layer — user exposes data gaps by torching 'Unknown Play' tags; (2) Lens Layer — Swarm-Sight portal reveals the Woodland Council cognitive roles (Owls audit, Foxes trap, Bunnies fuel morale) actively processing the gap; (3) Echo Layer — user briefly conducts the swarm via virtual baton, amplifying one AI voice and watching real calculations shift. Each layer is anchored by live statistical validation. Exit artifact: downloadable Sovereign's Sigil. The framework converts a product demo into a recruitment ritual.

evolving_frameworks.name: Chaos-Credibility Multiplication Model
evolving_frameworks.description: Rejects the additive model (credibility + chaos = diluted message) in favor of a multiplicative one: theatrical methodology visualization × hard data anchors = cognitive dissonance that enterprise buyers cannot ignore. The prospect expects boring SaaS; instead they get a fellowship-trained physician orchestrating AI swarms. Surprise × proof = memorable differentiation. Claude's 'Credibility Anchor' and Gemini's 'Swarm-Sight Lens' are the two required components — neither works without the other.

evolving_frameworks.name: Apostle Conversion Funnel
evolving_frameworks.description: Visitors enter as skeptical prospects, pass through the interactive crucible (Wand → Lens → Echo), and exit as apostles carrying a personalized Sovereign's Sigil. The funnel has three exit states: (1) Converted Client — books a demo after the interactive experience; (2) Evangelist — downloads and shares the Sigil without converting yet; (3) Rejected — leaves, but has been exposed to the methodology and may return. Success metric is not just direct conversion but Sigil propagation as a viral credibility artifact.

evolving_frameworks.name: Publication-First Commercialization Ladder
evolving_frameworks.description: Phase 1 (Research): Read-only CDS display, centralized cloud, immutable logging — optimized for trial integrity and landmark publication. Phase 2 (Post-Publication): Smart Phrase insertion, hybrid hosting — optimized for adoption. Phase 3 (Scale): FHIR write-back, on-prem options — optimized for enterprise deployment. Each phase unlocks the next by producing the evidence base required for the subsequent ask.

evolving_frameworks.name: Provable Ephemerality Stack
evolving_frameworks.description: Layered architecture for demonstrating — not just claiming — zero data retention: stateless containers with TTL enforcement → cryptographic session keys → automated destruction on termination → immutable audit log of destruction events. Each layer provides independent proof to a different audience (compliance officer, CMIO, payer auditor).

evolving_frameworks.name: Benchmark Positioning Triangle
evolving_frameworks.description: Three vertices that together constitute a field benchmark claim: (1) Evidence Gap — no published unified CDS pilots in urgent care; (2) Validated Safety — 0% hallucinations/coding gaps meeting DECIDE-AI/STARD-AI/AMIA; (3) Equity Hook — 43% higher denial odds for lowest-income patients. All three must be present simultaneously for the benchmark claim to be defensible against CMIO, compliance, and payer adversaries.

evolving_frameworks.name: Adversarial Attack Surface Map
evolving_frameworks.description: Four adversary archetypes with distinct primary attack vectors: CMIO attacks sample size (N=108, single site); Compliance Officer attacks PHI exposure surface (de-ID pipeline, session persistence); Epic Analyst attacks integration complexity (App Orchard certification, FHIR scope); Payer attacks ROI generalizability (pilot-to-scale denial reduction). Each architecture choice should be evaluated against all four vectors, not just the primary one.

evolving_frameworks.name: Orthogonal Moat Theory
evolving_frameworks.description: Two distinct competitive dimensions: Scale Moat (compute, data, parameters — owned by big labs) and Coordination Moat (routing logic, cross-validation, failure-mode doctrine, domain-grounded validation, auditability — owned by orchestration layer). Progress on the Scale Moat does not erode the Coordination Moat; in fact it strengthens it by expanding available model inventory. Disruption occurs when Coordination Moat captures enough downstream value that Scale Moat providers become interchangeable commodity components.

evolving_frameworks.name: Cost-Per-Outcome vs. Cost-Per-Call
evolving_frameworks.description: Two-tier cost analysis for AI systems: Call Cost (per-query API spend, where multi-model orchestration is 4-13x more expensive than single-model) vs. Outcome Cost (cost per solved, defensible, auditable result, where orchestration wins by reducing hallucination cleanup, re-queries, and downstream human correction cycles). The competitive claim for orchestration only holds at the Outcome Cost tier; using Call Cost framing inverts the argument.

evolving_frameworks.name: Fitness Function Divergence
evolving_frameworks.description: Systems optimized for benchmark performance (demo-land fitness) vs. systems optimized for messy-reality deployment (warzone fitness) are different in kind, not degree. Benchmark fitness selects for confidence and fluency. Warzone fitness selects for graceful degradation, safe failure, and auditability. The founding-under-fire origin story is not decoration — it is evidence that the system was shaped by a different selection pressure than competitor systems, producing architecturally distinct failure modes and recovery behaviors.

evolving_frameworks.name: Neutrality Trap
evolving_frameworks.description: The structural reason incumbents cannot replicate vendor-neutral orchestration: any single-vendor AI company that routes work to a competitor when the competitor performs better is (a) admitting their model is not always best, (b) subsidizing a competitor's improvement loop, and (c) printing its own lock-in breakup letter. Neutrality is therefore not a feature they can add — it is a posture that is incompatible with their business model. The Neutrality Trap means the orchestration layer can only be built by an entity with no model to protect.
